title: The Ophan's beams: three questions
eyebrow: Design area: the demand loop · the Ophan's arrival (#418), part 2 · nothing built

short.lead: Your answers make the Ophan a celestial threat. It appears in the sky, larger than life, and strikes with beams of light after a set lock-on delay, with no chase and no catch. That leaves three things about the beam itself undecided. They're below, each with my suggestion marked. One check first: I read "menstrual hum" as "monstrous hum". Say so if you meant something else.
short.hint: Tap a card for what's already settled or what one question decides.
items: Your answers from the first page
It arrives 60 seconds before the portal closes, only on raids where a demand is due or owed.
It appears in the sky, larger than life, and stays there. It never chases and never walks.
It attacks with beams of light after a set lock-on delay.
It targets whoever carries the most.
Until the demand exists, any piece marked as an artifact counts as wanted.
After a kill, it keeps hunting the others until the portal closes.
Its warning is a loud, monstrous hum and screen shake.
Nothing from you, unless I've misread the hum.
1. What a beam does to you
Whether one beam kills you or only hurts you.
What you can do during the lock-on delay, and how long it lasts.
Your rule is that carrying the wanted piece means it takes the piece and you live. With beams, it needs a new shape.

choices: hit
What does a beam do to an empty-handed player it hits?
A
Kills them outright
Matches "caught empty-handed, you die", and keeps it an overwhelming threat.
B
Heavy damage, so two hits kill
A second chance, which makes it a little less overwhelming.
C
Your own answer
Tell me what it does.
It keeps your rule that empty-handed means death, and keeps the threat celestial.
escape
During the lock-on delay, how do you escape?
A
Get under a roof or behind cover before it fires; the beam needs a clear line to the sky. Delay: 3 seconds
The castle's roofs and doorways become shelter, and the delay is one number in the tuning file.
B
Move: the beam strikes where you stood when it locked on. Delay: 2 seconds
Dodging becomes a skill, and roofs don't matter.
C
Your own answer
Tell me how, and how long the delay is.
Hiding from something in the sky reads at once, and it turns the castle itself into what saves you.
take
When it targets someone carrying the wanted piece, what happens?
A
The beam lifts the piece out of their hands into the sky; they live, and it leaves
Your rule stays as it is: one holder saves everyone.
B
The carrier must hold the piece up to the sky to offer it
Paying becomes a choice the player makes, and it never takes the piece by force.
C
Your own answer
Tell me how it takes it.
It keeps "it takes the piece and you live" with no new rules to learn.

wrapup.summary: Three questions about the Ophan's beams: what a hit does, how to escape a lock-on, and how it takes the piece.
wrapup.changing: Nothing is built yet. Your first-page answers are recorded in the design notes.
wrapup.blocking: Your answers to the three choices, and a word if I misread the hum.
wrapup.next: Once you answer, I update #418 to match and build it on its own branch, warning included, then test it and merge it into staging.
